title: `icons`
description: An optional array of display icons on a tool definition, each with a source URL, MIME type and size list.
question: Does the tool's icon set reach the agent's tool definition?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers declaring tool icons. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Icons are the one part of a tool definition aimed at a human rather than a model. A framework that drops them removes the server's only way to identify its tools visually in any UI built on top of the adapter.

notes.crewai: CrewAI: `crewai_tools` contains no reference to `icons` anywhere in the package, so the field has nowhere to survive adaptation.
notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `createDynamicTool` builds the Genkit tool from the MCP tool's `name` (prefixed `<server>/`), `description` and `inputSchema` only, with `outputSchema: z.any()` and `metadata: { mcp: { _meta } }`; `icons` does not survive.
notes.langchain: LangChain: `langchain_mcp_adapters` contains no reference to `icons`. `StructuredTool.metadata` carries annotations but no icon set.
notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK: the `agents` package contains no reference to `icons`. `FunctionTool` keeps `_mcp_title` only.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI: `pydantic_ai.mcp` declares `icons: list[Icon] | None` on its resource type only. `ToolDefinition` has no icon field, so tool icons are dropped.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: `@mastra/mcp` types `icons` under resource and configuration shapes. No tool type carries it, and the tool action's `mcp` metadata holds annotations only.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: retained on `McpTool.raw_mcp_tool.icons`; `FunctionDeclaration` has no icon field.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): toolsFromDefinitions reads name, title, description, inputSchema, annotations and _meta from each listed tool. `icons` is not copied onto the tool object, so it is dropped.
notes.ms_agent_framework: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `FunctionTool` has no icon field and `load_tools` does not read `icons`.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: `ToolSchema` has no icon field and `McpWorkbench` keeps no copy of the MCP tool.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPAgentTool.tool_spec` builds the `ToolSpec` from name, description, schemas and annotations. Icons stay on `MCPAgentTool.mcp_tool.icons` and never reach the spec the model receives.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `mcpToFunctionTool` builds the `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The tool's `icons` list is not on the tool the model is handed and is not kept anywhere beside it.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: icons are not read by `load_tools` and are not kept on the KernelFunction.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool` and `ToolMetadata` have no icon field, and the icons are not kept.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `FunctionDeclaration` has no icon field, and `MCPTool` keeps the icons only on its TypeScript-private `mcpTool` field.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools.build_tools` registers each tool as `Function(name, description, parameters=inputSchema)`; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are not carried, so `icons` are discarded.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` builds each `haystack.tools.Tool` from the tool's name, description and `inputSchema` only, so `icons` does not reach the tool definition.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt builds each `MCPAdaptTool` from the name, description and `inputSchema` properties only, and neither `smolagents.Tool` nor the function-tool dict has an icon field, so the icons are not kept.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: `Tool.from_mcp_tool` builds a `dspy.Tool` from the MCP tool's name, description and `inputSchema` properties only; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are on no `Tool` field and in no dict the LM is handed, so `icons` are discarded.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `icons` is not carried onto the `DynamicStructuredTool` or its metadata, so neither the provider tool nor the application can read it.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: `SyncMcpToolCallbackProvider` builds a `ToolDefinition`, which holds only a name, a description and the input schema, so `icons` is dropped.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `icons` is dropped; the MCP `Tool` survives only on the private `MCPTool._tool`.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): `icons` are not carried onto the provider tool or kept anywhere the session exposes.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient._list_tools_impl` keeps only the name, description and `inputSchema` of each tool, and neither `MCPNativeTool` nor the OpenAI function schema has an icon field, so the icons are not kept.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpTool` keeps the MCP tool's annotations and `_meta`, not its `icons`; the `FunctionDeclaration` has no place for them.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: tool `icons` reach `ToolSpecification.metadata()` only, so they never reach the `ChatModel`.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `icons` are dropped. The `ToolDescriptor` has no icon field and `McpTool` does not keep the SDK `Tool`.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `convertTool` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only, and `mcpTool` keeps no other field of the `*mcp.Tool`, so `icons` is gone after listing.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): `icons` stay on the public `McpClientTool.ProtocolTool` (framework metadata); the `AIFunction` the model is given has no place for them.
